column2: A narrow sea inlet between steep, rocky cliffs, as if nature had carved through the mountains with a giant knife.
A small disc used as a counter in casino games, or a tiny piece broken off a china cup.
A fiercely reactive chemical element — the unruly ancestor of the fluoride in your toothpaste.
A player skilled with the ball at his feet, who occasionally collapses onto the pitch with theatrical flair.
A loose, comfortable garment worn around the house when relaxation has officially defeated ceremony.
A scientist studying substances and their reactions — someone who knows why mixing random lab bottles is a terrible idea.
The crisp, satisfying snap of something brittle being chewed — the signature soundtrack of fresh celery and biscuits.
Any single numeral from zero to nine, without which a calculator has nothing to display.
A tangy preserve made from bitter Seville oranges and shredded peel — the undisputed monarch of the British breakfast toast.
A distinctive trait or part of the face that sets one person or thing apart from the rest.
An aquatic plant bearing horned, floating nuts — a quirky edible curiosity of slow rivers and ponds.
A fitted cabinet with shelves and doors where everything that 'might come in useful one day' goes to live.
A thin, round bread made from simple dough, serving as an edible plate across the Caucasus and Central Asia.
A simple, temporary hideout built from branches and leaves — the classic architecture of childhood woodland adventures.
The groom's trusted right-hand man at a wedding, tasked with keeping the ceremony on track — and not losing the rings.
A worker who extracts coal or ore deep underground, spending the working day well below street level.
The side of a formation or team; the quarter from which the most unexpected move sometimes arrives.
Light, coquettish exchange; a kind of verbal tennis in which the smile matters more than the serve.
A garden flower with scented clusters of blooms; a summer resident of the flowerbed, fond of arriving in company.
The plant life of a given region; the whole green company of a district, no guest list required.
A body of warships or merchant vessels; a transport force whose roads are made of water.
A flat vessel for water or a drink; the walking companion that has known every sort of weather.
An obsessive, overpowering fear; anxiety that sometimes declares even a harmless spider dangerous.
The shape or outward appearance of a thing; also the prescribed set of clothes — one word for a figure and a school outfit alike.
A small defended structure; a castle of compact format but serious intentions.
A place for discussion; where a three-line question can summon three hundred replies.
A quantum of electromagnetic radiation; a tiny portion of light that travels without luggage.
A complete, or nearly self-contained, stretch of speech; a few words able to alter the mood of a conversation.
A man's formal garment, cut short at the front and long behind; dress in which even standing becomes ceremonial — the uniform of white tie.
A man fussily devoted to dress and manners; one who treats a walk to the shops as a public appearance.
A rotating cutting tool for shaping materials; its many edges remove the surplus without sentiment.
The forward line of fighting, or a direction of work; where events unfold with particular urgency.
A musical form in which short themes enter in turn and interweave with skill; a conversation in music without interruptions — Bach preferred it that way.
A tall stemmed glass for wine or something sparkling; tableware that knows how to chime on festive occasions.
A large goods vehicle, usually drawing a trailer; a road giant for whom an ordinary courtyard is a tight fit.
A team game with a ball, the object being to put it in the other side's net rather than argue with the referee.
A specialist in unorthodox ways into computer systems; a digital explorer with a reputation for heroics or villainy.
A small sea fish, usually sold salted or canned; a little maritime guest with a big flavour.
A ruler's title among several peoples of the East; a post nobody was ever awarded for good behaviour.
A simple rural dwelling; a house of folk character and solid walls.
The rear part of an animal's body, or the trail of something; sometimes an ornament, sometimes a reason to keep up.
A spore-bearing plant with jointed stems; a green antique that remembers the dinosaurs.
The pointed foliage of coniferous trees; the green dress that does not fall off the autumn schedule.
A fortified grape wine from Spain; a drink of matured character and a protected home address — and the soul of the trifle.
The science of substances, their make-up, properties and transformations; it explains what happens when the wrong bottles get mixed.
A bitter substance historically used against malaria; a medicine whose character is felt on the tongue — and in the gin and tonic.
A physician who treats disease and injury by operation; the specialist whose work demands a particularly steady hand.
A popular song or work; the tune that moves into the head and never pays rent.
A sturdy organic substance forming the external skeleton of arthropods; nature's armour for insects.
Ancient Greek dress in the shape of a long tunic; classical attire without zips or pockets.
The staple food made of flour and water; the food for which many households still walk to the shop daily.
A building for keeping livestock; the rural lodging whose tenants ask for neither en-suite nor broadband.
A chemical element with a sharp smell, used to make water safe; the sanitary guardian of swimming pools.
A natural dye from a plant, used to colour hair and to paint temporary patterns on the skin.
The long, mobile nose of the elephant, serving at once as hand, shower and food-gathering tool.
The patch of an animal's back between neck and shoulder blades; the spot by which a horse's height is judged.
A spacious room at the entrance of a building; the zone of meetings, waiting and stray suitcases.
A modest rise in the landscape; a mountain that decided against showing off.
A low temperature, or the sensation of chill; the condition in which the blanket is suddenly promoted to best friend.
The stout fabric of painting; the surface on which an artist turns emptiness into an idea.
A small rodent with cheek pouches; the household storekeeper who carries the supplies off in its own pockets.
A company of singers performing together; the team whose whole art lies in landing on the same note.
A small predator with a supple body and an inquiring mind; the domestic explorer of every gap and crevice.
Loud, unstoppable laughter; a sound difficult to switch off even after the joke has been explained.
A religious building for worship; a place where the architecture often speaks in symbols.
The male of the domestic pig; a sturdy figure of the farmyard with a very recognisable voice.
A group of officers who have seized power; a regime that rarely arrives by the ordinary ballot.
A sweet orange fruit, astringent until properly ripe; an autumn dessert with a will of its own.
A separate small rural settlement or farm; an address for those who prefer the silence of the fields to the neighbours' group chat.
The fragrant outer layer of citrus peel; the thin strip that lends baking a sunny character.
A soft alkali metal, among the most reactive elements known; a substance for which water is no friend at all.
What one strives for; the destination point for which plans are drawn up and, occasionally, a diary is bought.
The money expression of a good's or service's value; the figure on the ticket that can spoil the romance of the purchase.
A row of connected metal links; a structure that holds fast and dislikes weak elements.
A sequence of repeating stages or events; the roundabout that reliably delivers one back to the start.
The illness brought on by long deficiency of vitamin C; the historic affliction of sailors short of fresh fruit — the Royal Navy's citrus order changed all that.
A metal used to shield steel from corrosion; the invisible bodyguard of ironwork.
A quick, ringing sound of hooves or heels; the acoustic announcement that somebody is approaching.
A sugared piece of fruit or citrus rind; the sweet way summer is kept in a jar — and smuggled into the Christmas cake.
A member of a European nation with its own language and a centuries-old culture; the neutral modern name of this people — its older common label has fallen out of polite use.
A growth on the birch formed by a fungus; woodland raw material, often brewed as a drink.
A woman's wrap covering body and head; traditional dress of women in some Muslim cultures.
A headwrap of long cloth wound about the head; an accessory of impressive architecture.
A large vessel for water or other liquids; the capacious container of household and laundry affairs.
A unit of time equal to sixty minutes; a stretch that lasts especially long in a queue.
A separate fragment of a whole; the piece of a common structure without which everything sometimes falls to bits.
A deep vessel without a handle; the tableware of drinks, prizes and symbolic rites.
Dense, hard-going woodland; a green labyrinth in which the path is clearly not a priority.
The document confirming a purchase or payment; the paper proof that the money has indeed gone.
A strand of hair falling over the forehead; the haircut that may obscure the eyes but never the mood.
A small boat, often hollowed from a single tree trunk; water transport with a minimalist hull.
A member of the species Homo sapiens; the creature that built spacecraft and still mislays its keys.
A woman's headwear covering the hair; an old accessory of tidy fit — and, in Britain, the same word for the front of a car.
A removable shell for protecting an object; the clothing of telephones, furniture and suitcases.
The small plates covering fish and certain reptiles; nature's armour, with a polish.
A wading bird with a crest and striking plumage; dressed as though for a formal reception — the British know it by its cry, the peewit.
A herbaceous plant of the pea family; a cousin of the garden pea, with flowers and tendrils.
A mathematical notion of quantity or order; the answer to 'how many?' achieved without the fingers.
One who reads a text aloud with expression; the voice that brings even the microwave instructions to life.
A lock of hair at the crown or the brow; the strand that aspires to rise above the rest — and was once tugged by way of greeting.
An inner experience, or the capacity to perceive; that which no ruler can fully measure.
An odd, unconventional sort; one who walks their own road without consulting society's manual — in Britain, practically a national category.
A single movement of the leg in walking; the minimal unit of the road to a great aim.
A child or person given to mischief; the specialist in locating where the boundaries lie.
The possibility of success, or of turning events around; a door that sometimes opens once.
A head covering worn against cold or sun; the accessory which regularly goes missing at the least convenient moment.
A comic likeness with the sitter's features exaggerated; a portrait that has slightly overdone the truth.
A particular allure and appeal; a quality independent of looks, and one almost never discounted.
A person with hair of brown shades; the owner of a colour between blond and dark.
A board game of sixteen pieces a side; a battle of minds in which the pawn occasionally becomes the star.
A board game with round counters on a chequered board; the strategy in which the humblest piece may be crowned king.
A native of Scandinavia's largest kingdom; a person from the land of northern forests and understated design.
A craftsperson who makes and mends clothing; the specialist who can make the fabric behave.
A whipped drink of milk, ice cream or fruit; the dessert that prefers a glass and a straw.
An honorific title in Arab countries for a chief, elder or religious figure; an address with historical weight.
The fine natural fibre spun by the caterpillar that feeds on mulberry leaves; the fabric that manages to look luxurious without raising its voice.
